projects.title: FreeSpace 2
projects.description: A native Switch port of the open-source engine for FreeSpace 2.
projects.releaseNotes:
## v1.0.1

- fix pilot-menu crash, touch scaling and on-screen keyboard


INSTALL
-------

Create the folder  sdmc:/switch/freespace2/  on your SD card and put the .nro
and all of your game data together in it:

    sdmc:/switch/freespace2/
        freespace2.nro          <- this release
        root_fs2.vp             \
        sparky_fs2.vp            |  your FreeSpace 2 data
        sparky_hi_fs2.vp        |  (every *.vp file)
        ... (all other *.vp)    /
        Data/
            Movies/             <- cutscenes (*.mve), optional


CONFIGURATION
-------------

On first launch a config.txt is created next to the .nro :

    rumble = 1              (HD rumble: 1 = on, 0 = off)
    gyro = 0               (motion aiming while flying: 1 = on, 0 = off)
    gyro_sensitivity = 50   (gyro strength: 0-100)

CONTROLS
--------

    Left stick    Fly (pitch / roll)
    Right stick   Throttle / rudder       (menus: move cursor)
    A / ZR        Fire primary            (menus: select)
    B / ZL        Fire secondary          (menus: back)
    R             Afterburner
    X             Launch countermeasure
    Y             Target ship in reticle
    L             Target nearest enemy
    D-pad         Arrow keys
    +  (Plus)     Pause / in-mission menu
    -  (Minus)    On-screen keyboard (e.g. to enter a pilot name)
projects.note: Requires files from your own legally obtained copy. Follow the project’s guide for the exact version and setup.

## Downloads

| For | File |
|---|---|
| Windows, installer | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Windows-x86_64-Setup.exe` |
| Windows, portable (unzip and open `SafeHouse.exe`) | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Windows-x86_64-Portable.zip` |
| Windows on ARM, installer | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Windows-arm64-Setup.exe` |
| Windows on ARM, portable | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Windows-arm64-Portable.zip` |
| Linux and Steam Deck, AppImage | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux, archive | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Linux on ARM (Steam Frame), AppImage | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Linux-aarch64.AppImage` |
| Linux on ARM, archive | `SafeHouse-Launcher-Linux-aarch64.tar.gz` |
| macOS, Apple silicon | `SafeHouse-Launcher-macOS-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `SafeHouse-Launcher-macOS-x86_64.dmg` |
| Nintendo Switch (homebrew, copy to `sdmc:/switch/SafeHouse/`) | `SafeHouse.nro` |

The launcher updates itself (Settings > Launcher > Check for updates). SHA-256 checksums are in `SHA256SUMS`.
On macOS, open the app with right-click > Open the first time. The packages contain no game data.

projects.title: Autorun
projects.description: Runs Windows games and programs on Nintendo Switch using Wine and CPU translation. Previously known as Wine-NX.
projects.releaseNotes:
**Install:** delete old autorun installation, unzip `autorun-test-build-4.zip` to the **root of your SD card** — everything goes into `switch/wine`. 

**What changed, how to upgrade from test-build-3 and known issues:** see the release thread on the forum:
[https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/101/autorun-test-build-4](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/101/autorun-test-build-4)

Upgrading from test-build-3? Your Windows user folder is now `C:\users\steamuser` (was `C:\users\wine`): move saves and settings from `switch/wine/drive_c/users/wine` to `switch/wine/drive_c/users/steamuser`. The forum post has the details.

Game reports and help: [Game Discussion](https://forum.ticoverse.com/category/21/game-discussion) · [Help & Suggestions](https://forum.ticoverse.com/category/23/help-suggestions)

### Antivirus false positives

Some of the DLLs in this package are heavily patched Wine builds, modified so Wine can run on the Switch's OS at all. This can trip antivirus and scanner heuristics. That's a false positive caused by the patching, not malicious code — the source is in this repository if you want to check it or build it yourself.
projects.note: Experimental test build. Bring your own Windows game files and check the project’s installation and compatibility notes.
